title: Restriction of the finite-type kernel condition to an open subscheme
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $F$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Suppose that for every open $U\subseteq X$, every $n\in\mathbb N$ and every map $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to F|_U$, the kernel is of finite type in the sense of [pqf-def-coherent]. For an open $W\subseteq X$, restriction is as in [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]. Then for every open $V\subseteq W$, every $n\in\mathbb N$, and every map $\mathcal O_V^{\oplus n}\to (F|_W)|_V$, its kernel is of finite type. No finite-type hypothesis on $F$ is imposed.

source.place: Definitions 01BV (definition-coherent), 01B5 (definition-finite-type), and Section 01AF (section-kernels); read at the official Stacks tag pages

proof.text: Let V be open in W and let V prime be its image in X. It is open in X because W is open. The open-site equivalence and iterated-slice equivalence identify (F restricted to W) restricted to V with F restricted to V prime, and identify the structure modules.
These equivalences preserve finite coproducts and kernels. Transfer the given rank-n free-source map to the module category over V prime. Its kernel is finite type by the hypothesis on F.

Transport the kernel back to V. Transfer each finite family of local generating sections and its epimorphism along the equivalences. Corresponding open neighbourhoods cover, so finite type transfers. This proves the assertion, also for empty opens and rank zero.
